# Missing test cases

19 of 100 deliberate changes were not detected by the full ported upstream suite: 58 test-file tests plus 80 source doc tests (138 tests). This is a bounded mutation study. The 24 feature-gated doc examples could not be ported under the stable, import-only rules. No matching assertion for these witnesses was found by content review of the seven supplied upstream files or the extracted doc blocks. 

Whole-tree search (review, 2026-10-09): the 1.99.0 coretests and benches, library/std net unit tests and TCP/UDP tests, core doc tests outside net, tests/ui, Miri, Clippy and rustfmt tests were searched by content. No covering assertion for any of the 19 named witnesses was found. Std net unit tests and Miri were checked by reading; they were not run under the mutants. This content review does not establish universal test absence. Each proposed test passes on the restored copy and on real std 1.99.0. Each fails at runtime on its mutant. Error-text and Debug cases are optional representation regression tests. Exact outputs have no compatibility obligation. M095 separately records an unresolved Display policy.

The port includes 47 coretests, 11 std value-type tests and 80 doc tests. DNS, UDP and ToSocketAddrs tests are excluded; see [PORTING.md](PORTING.md). [DOC-TESTS.md](DOC-TESTS.md) records all 109 fenced blocks: 80 ported, 24 feature-gated unported, four non-Rust and one should_panic skipped as requested. All 138 ported tests stayed green for every row below. Exact names and output appear in each linked upstream log.

The earlier 23-case list is preserved in [Brief 2 history](../history/missing-tests-brief2-files-only.md). Doc tests now detect M001, M005, M013, M040. [SURVIVOR-REVIEW.md](SURVIVOR-REVIEW.md) records a content search and a non-equivalence witness for each remaining case. The review covers the whole-tree locations listed above. No equivalent survivor was found.

The final [native summary](evidence/intree/replay/summary.json) records 66 baseline core net tests passed; 19 applied; each detected only by the added tests; all 47 existing net coretests and 105 doc tests stay green; 0 skipped. Each mutant fails its own added test; M092 also fails the added Debug test. The other 18 fail only their own added test. No existing core net test fails. All 105 native doc tests pass per mutant. [Native evidence](evidence/intree/README.md) links the baseline and every per-mutant log. Earlier `intree/logs/b` receipts are historical.

The main [coretests patch](coretests-net.patch) contains 12 behavioural cases covering 7 distinct behaviours; the six leading-whitespace cases are one rule. The [optional patch](coretests-net-optional.patch) contains 7 representation snapshots. The FromStr impls are heavily tested in coretests `parser.rs:25–110` and `ip_addr.rs:9–120`; only the named behaviours are missing. The native baseline predates the split and contains all 19 additions (47 + 12 + 7 = 66). Both split patches pass applicability checks and their added tests pass on real std; no native x run was performed for the split.

### M073: SocketAddrV6 FromStr: parses the maximum numeric scope id

Clamp numeric IPv6 scopes to u32::MAX minus one.

[Upstream green](evidence/gen/M073-upstream.txt), [new test red](evidence/gen/M073-proposed.txt), [copy green](evidence/gen/M073-baseline.txt), [real std green](evidence/gen/proposed-real-std.txt).

```rust
// generated by Codex gpt-6.1-sol on 2026-10-07 for Ivo Matijasevic
use core::net::*;

#[test]
fn test_m073_scope_max() {
    assert_eq!("[::1%4294967295]:0".parse::<SocketAddrV6>().unwrap().scope_id(),u32::MAX);
}
```

## Optional representation regression tests

The six error-text and Debug snapshots are optional. No supplied contract guarantees the exact AddrParseError sentence. `core/src/fmt/mod.rs` says exactly: “Additionally, `Debug` implementations of types provided by the standard library (`std`, `core`, `alloc`, etc.) are not stable, and may also change with future Rust versions.” The five constant-output Debug controls are non-equivalent but give limited information about formatting coverage. M095 is also optional: it observes an unresolved translated-prefix Display policy.

### M095: Ipv6Addr Display: translated-prefix hexadecimal snapshot (optional)

Display only the full RFC 2765 translated prefix in mixed notation, retaining all payload octets.

[Upstream green](evidence/gen/M095-upstream.txt), [new test red](evidence/gen/M095-proposed.txt), [copy green](evidence/gen/M095-baseline.txt), [real std green](evidence/gen/proposed-real-std.txt).

```rust
// generated by Codex gpt-6.1-sol on 2026-10-07 for Ivo Matijasevic
use core::net::*;

#[test]
fn test_m095_rfc5952_5_translated() {
    assert_eq!("::ffff:0:192.0.2.1".parse::<Ipv6Addr>().unwrap().to_string(),"::ffff:0:c000:201");
}
```

The full six-segment translated prefix alone changes to mixed notation, retaining the low 32-bit payload. The hexadecimal expectation is an optional representation regression test of the current Display policy. It does not assert RFC 5952 recommendation compliance. The final [native M095 log](evidence/intree/replay/M095-coretests.txt) confirms detection only by its own added test; [native doc tests](evidence/intree/replay/M095-doctests.txt) remain green. The earlier copied native log is historical and exercises the superseded mutant.
